clue.text: The height of classical Greek architecture?

definitions.text: The height of classical Greek architecture?

parts.words: The height of classical Greek architecture?
parts.note: read literally, the 'high city' of ancient Athens, its hilltop citadel crowned with temples, is the very top of Greek building

explanation.surface: A question about the peak achievement of ancient Greek building style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Height' seems to mean the high point of an artistic period, but it is literal: the name means 'upper city', a fortified hilltop with the Parthenon on it.
explanation.definitionFit: The citadel of Athens stands on a high rock and carries the finest classical Greek temples.

clue.text: Lost after temperature rises in one constituency

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means a letter climbs towards the top, so the temperature letter moves earlier

parts.note: one is A, and a constituency is a parliamentary seat

explanation.surface: An election candidate loses after the political temperature heats up in a single district.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rises' moves the T of A SEAT up (earlier) to give AT SEA.
explanation.definitionFit: Being all at sea idiomatically means bewildered, out of one's depth.

clue.text: What's left of article with, say, knot tied around it

indicators.note: 'it' points back to the article, so the reminder phrase is placed round that letter

parts.note: a knot tied in a handkerchief is an example ('say') of a memory prompt, a reminder
A is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A piece about leftovers, with a knot tied around the item.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around it' puts A inside REMINDER, giving REM-A-INDER.
explanation.definitionFit: The remainder is the portion still left over once the rest has been taken.

clue.text: Badly typecast, husband is ready for minor roles

indicators.note: badly signals the word typecast is jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: An actor poorly typecast, with her husband, is ready to take small parts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Badly' is the anagram signal. 'Ready' is old slang for cash, and petty cash pays for small items, the 'minor roles' of money, though the surface suggests an actor's bit parts.
explanation.definitionFit: Ready means cash, and petty cash is the money kept for small, minor expenses.

clue.text: Editorial work seen in theatrical anthology

definitions.text: Editorial work seen in theatrical anthology

parts.words: Editorial work seen in theatrical anthology
parts.note: newspaper opinion pieces, read whimsically as star roles (leading) and items (articles) in a collection of plays

explanation.surface: An editor's work turning up in a collection of plays.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is 'Editorial'; the rest suggests the main pieces in a book of theatre, playing on 'leading' as in a leading role.
explanation.definitionFit: Editorials in a British newspaper are also called leaders, the paper's main opinion pieces.

clue.text: Many contenders, oddly, outside ring act formally

indicators.note: outside means the jumbled letters wrap round the ring letter
oddly says the letters of the two words are arranged strangely

parts.note: a ring is round, so it gives the letter O

explanation.surface: Lots of rivals behave strangely outside the boxing ring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly' tempts a solver to take alternate letters, but here it shuffles MANY CONTENDERS, and 'outside' puts that round O.
explanation.definitionFit: To stand on ceremony is to insist on formal behaviour and etiquette.

clue.text: How to address woman in Mothers' Union?

parts.note: Ma is an informal word for mother
a dam is an animal's mother

explanation.surface: Asking the correct form of address for a woman in the Mothers' Union church charity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Union' joins two words for mother, MA and DAM. The Mothers' Union is a Christian women's charity in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Madam is the polite form of address used for a woman.

clue.text: Lead, for example, as director of agents and others

parts.note: M is the head of the secret service in the James Bond stories
et al is the Latin abbreviation meaning and others

explanation.surface: The lead role, played by the spymaster and the rest of the cast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lead' suggests the leading role; it is the heavy grey element.
explanation.definitionFit: Lead is one example of the class of metallic elements.

clue.text: Fellow holding me up, the fiend

indicators.note: holding means the fellow word contains the next piece

parts.note: a don is a fellow of a university college

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the letters are read bottom to top

explanation.surface: A man holding me aloft, the devil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses the clue's 'me' and 'holding' sets it inside the fellow; a don is a fellow (teacher) at an Oxford or Cambridge college.
explanation.definitionFit: A demon is an evil spirit or devil.

clue.text: It provides many openings for ship's captain on island

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means the second piece is placed after the first

parts.note: a master is the captain of a merchant ship
a key is a low island, as in the Florida Keys

explanation.surface: Job opportunities for a ship's captain on an island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'many openings' sounds like career chances, but means doors that one key unlocks.
explanation.definitionFit: A master key unlocks many different locks in a building.

clue.text: Buddhist writing about old lady in Eastern island

indicators.note: about means the writing goes round the old lady

parts.note: a sutra is a Buddhist scripture
old lady is slang for mother, Ma

explanation.surface: A Buddhist text about a grandmother living on an island in the East.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' signals the container; 'old lady' is British slang for one's mother.
explanation.definitionFit: Sumatra is a large island of Indonesia, in the East.

clue.text: Huntress in woods I met, rapidly retreating

indicators.note: retreating says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A huntress encountered in the forest, quickly backing away.
explanation.walkthrough: SIMETRA lies inside 'woodS I MET RApidly'; 'retreating' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: Artemis is the Greek goddess of hunting.

clue.text: Little woman embracing the object of friendship

indicators.note: embracing means the woman's name wraps around the next piece

parts.note: Amy is one of the four March sisters in Louisa May Alcott's novel Little Women
it is an object pronoun, a thing

explanation.surface: A small woman hugging the person she wants to befriend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'embracing' signals the container; capital-L 'Little woman' points to Alcott's novel, not a small person.
explanation.definitionFit: Amity is peaceful friendship and goodwill.

clue.text: Lack of activity, woefully on decline

indicators.note: woefully, meaning badly, signals that on decline is rearranged

explanation.surface: Being idle, sadly, leads to going downhill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'woefully' rearranges ON DECLINE.
explanation.definitionFit: Indolence is laziness, an avoidance of effort.

clue.text: Oil etc found in region near Caspian Sea

definitions.meaning: oil, watercolour and so on are the materials artists work in
an ancient land of the Medes, in what is now north-west Iran

explanation.surface: Oil and the like discovered near the Caspian.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests petroleum near Baku; 'oil' is the painter's material.
explanation.definitionFit: Artists' materials are their media, and the ancient kingdom of the Medes lay south-west of the Caspian.

clue.text: Silly emphasis on name being distorted

indicators.note: silly signals that emphasis is rearranged

explanation.surface: Daft stress on a name makes it come out wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Silly' is the anagram signal; 'distorted' looks like a further anagram indicator but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Something misshapen is deformed, out of its proper shape.

clue.text: Crew arrange with king way to get on board

parts.note: a gang is a crew of workers
to plan is to arrange
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: Sailors arrange with the king how to come aboard.
explanation.definitionFit: A gangplank is the movable walkway used to board a ship.

clue.text: Tsar crossing European border or boundary

indicators.note: crossing means the tsar's name lies across, around, the next pieces

parts.note: Peter the Great was a tsar of Russia
a rim is a border or edge

explanation.surface: A Russian ruler crossing a European frontier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crossing' signals the container; the tsar is Peter the Great, and the border and European pieces sit inside his name.
explanation.definitionFit: A perimeter is the outer boundary line of an area.

clue.text: Taking unorthodox stance, and upwardly mobile

indicators.note: unorthodox means not in the usual order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone adopting an unusual position while climbing socially.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unorthodox' rearranges STANCE AND.
explanation.definitionFit: Ascendant means rising, gaining in power or status.

clue.text: Increase covering daily addition to cost

indicators.note: covering means the increase word wraps round the next piece

parts.note: a surge is a sudden increase
a daily is a cleaning woman, a char in British usage

explanation.surface: A rise to pay for the daily cleaner adds to the bill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'covering' signals the container. A 'daily' or char is British for a cleaner who comes in each day.
explanation.definitionFit: A surcharge is an extra fee added on top of the price.

clue.text: Unstable fighter making many comebacks

definitions.meaning: the boxer ... Balboa returns in film after film of the Sylvester Stallone series

explanation.surface: A shaky boxer who keeps returning to the ring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'comebacks' are the film sequels as much as returns to the ring.
explanation.definitionFit: Rocky means shaky, and Rocky Balboa is Stallone's much-sequelled boxer.

clue.text: Abusing race, I'm the offender in this

definitions.text: Abusing race, I'm the offender in this

indicators.note: abusing means misusing, so the following letters are mistreated into a new order

explanation.surface: A racist offender confesses to their crime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Abusing' rearranges RACE IM THE; the whole clue then describes the offence.
explanation.definitionFit: Racial abuse is a classic example of an offence motivated by prejudice.

clue.text: Change direction in boat covering right course

indicators.note: covering means the sailing word wraps round the next piece

parts.note: to tack is to turn a sailing boat into the wind

explanation.surface: Turning a boat to the right to stay on course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'covering' puts R inside TACK.
explanation.definitionFit: A track is a path or route, a course to follow.

clue.text: Rabble taking away ship and gold from this, for example

indicators.note: taking away says letters are removed
from names the word that the letters are removed from

parts.note: the puzzle being solved is an example of a crossword
SS stands for steamship
or is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: A mob stealing a ship and its gold treasure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'this' points to the puzzle itself: remove SS and OR from CROSSWORD to leave CROWD.
explanation.definitionFit: A rabble is a disorderly crowd of people.

clue.text: Champ who put one screaming on the canvas?

definitions.meaning: to champ is to chew noisily

definitions.text: who put one screaming on the canvas?
definitions.meaning: the Norwegian painter of The Scream, a figure screaming painted on canvas

explanation.surface: A boxing champion who knocked a yelling opponent down onto the canvas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Champ' looks like a boxing champion and 'canvas' the ring floor, but it is chewing and a painting.
explanation.definitionFit: To munch is to chew steadily, and Edvard Munch painted The Scream.

clue.text: Person on walkabout greeting king and queen

parts.note: hi is a greeting
K is the chess abbreviation for king
ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: A royal on a walkabout, greeting the king and queen.
explanation.walkthrough: A royal 'walkabout' is meeting the crowds; here it is just a walk.
explanation.definitionFit: A hiker is someone who goes on long country walks.

clue.text: Exercises a fine bird, one from Asia

parts.note: PE stands for physical education, exercises
F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencils
an owl is a bird

explanation.surface: Working out a fine bird that comes from Asia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bird' seems part of the definition, but it is the OWL; the definition is 'one from Asia', a bird native there.
explanation.definitionFit: Peafowl, the peacock and peahen, are native to India and South-East Asia.

clue.text: Combine parts of return journey in remote region

parts.note: a round trip goes out, the outward leg
and comes back, the homeward leg

explanation.surface: Merging both legs of a round trip into one in the wilderness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Combine' joins OUT and BACK, the two legs of an out-and-back journey.
explanation.definitionFit: The outback is the remote, sparsely populated interior of Australia.

clue.text: Stark negative response of Scots to King Edward

parts.note: na is Scots for no
Ed is short for Edward

explanation.surface: A Scottish refusal, bluntly, to King Edward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stark' looks like an adjective for the refusal, but is the definition, as in stark naked.
explanation.definitionFit: Stark, as in stark naked, means completely bare or nude.

clue.text: Creator of advertising whose work is highly regarded

definitions.text: Creator of advertising whose work is highly regarded

parts.words: Creator of advertising whose work is highly regarded
parts.note: an aerial advertiser whose messages, traced in smoke, are looked up at overhead

explanation.surface: An admired advertising creative.
explanation.walkthrough: 'highly regarded' seems to mean admired, but means literally looked at high up.
explanation.definitionFit: A pilot tracing smoke letters overhead writes adverts that people gaze up at.
